paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples with a larger number of examples
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how the metric **minFDE\_20 (←)** varies with the **Number of Examples**, showing two methods labeled **ST-ES** and **Random**. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Examples,” uses a linear scale, and spans integer values from **0 to 15**, with major tick labels shown at **0, 5, 10, and 15**. The y-axis is labeled “minFDE\_20 (←),” uses a linear scale, and ranges roughly from just under **16** up to **22**, with regularly spaced tick labels at **16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, and 22**. The **ST-ES** series is drawn as a **blue solid line** with **circular markers**, starting near **22.0** at **0** examples, dropping to about **16.8** at **1**, then moving gradually around the low-16 range for the remainder (e.g., about **16.1** at **5**, approximately **16.0** at **6–7**, a small bump near **16.15** at **8**, and ending around **16.1** at **15**). The **Random** series is an **orange solid line** with **circular markers**, starting near **21.9** at **0**, decreasing to around **20.7** at **1**, then staying close to the mid-20 range with small fluctuations (e.g., about **20.35–20.55** across **3–10**, around **20.40** at **11–14**), and ending near **20.45** at **15**.
